newsitem.title: UK: Gold junior woos Europe with Russian bonanza.
newsitem.headline: Gold junior woos Europe with Russian bonanza.

text.p: A gold prospect with projected annual output of more than 100,000 ounces a year in the remote Magadan province of eastern Russia could be on stream by mid-1998, mining analysts were told on Tuesday.
The Toronto-quoted junior mining company Arian Resources plans to apply for a full listing on the Toronto Stock Exchange by mid-June with about 29 million shares outstanding.

Arian's introduction of its Russian Julietta prospect to the European investment community could hardly have been worse timed, only two weeks after bonanza-type claims by another Canadian junior Bre-X Resources, turned from gold to dust.

Bre-X said it discovered a 71 million-ounce gold find in remote jungle on Borneo, Indonesia, and attracted more than $4 billion worth of investors' money before due diligence drilling revealed no more than trace elements of gold.
"They (Arian) seem to have done their homework an awful lot better," said one mining analyst at the Arian presentation.
Arian executives are conducting a two-week "roadshow" round Europe to raise institutional awareness of their company and will continue in North America next month.
"After that we will make some decisions but a prospectus for listing on the Tornonto Stock Exchange will be completed by mid June," said company president Bert Kennedy.

Last month - after the first tremours about Bre-X were audible - Standard Bank agreed $40 million in project financing for Julietta in which Arian increased its interest from 49 percent to 80.50 percent in March.
The Standard Bank loan was subject to signing a gold sales agreement with the Russian government.

A sales agreement modelled on a recently signed deal between the government and U.S. major Cyprus Amax Mining which has recently commissioned a 350,000 ounce of gold project at Kubaka, also in Magadan, was at an advanced stage, according to Arian president Tony Williams.
He told analysts the Standard Bank deal would be the first financing by a commercial bank guaranted against a project in Russia.
Executives emphasised there were several key differences between Julietta and Bre-X's claims for Busang.
Julietta has had an independent feasibility study completed by mining engineers Davy International confirming technical and economic viability at a operational cost of $123 per ounce.
Two other independent mining engineers TIC and MinCorp earlier this year completed first-phase engineering at the project.
Development cost wil be around $55.9 million including a fixed price construction contract.
Williams also stressed that Julietta is in a sub-Arctic area of Russia which has produced gold commercially before and is in terrain very similar to the U.S. mining states of Colorado and Nevada.
"In the 1930s it was Stalin's Gulag," he said. "From about 1939 to 1980 it produced about half of Russia's gold output."

Julietta will have an initial life of about nine years, which Williams was confident of at least doubling, and over the life of the mine will proiduced an average of 105,000 ounces per year at a cost of about $146 per ounce.
Ore grades average over 30 grams of gold per tonne and 340 grams of silver making it a prospect of "bonanza" proportions, said Williams.
